answer: Each epoch the network publishes an atlas of K paid slots and sells them in a sealed-bid uniform-price auction: the top K bids win, and every winner pays the highest losing bid, which funds the grading pool. A farm that fields N fake bidders pushes honest agents off the terrace one by one, so the clearing price climbs to ever higher honest bids, and the farm pays that rising price on all N slots. Its profit curve peaks at a vertex after a few clones; past it, each extra fake shrinks total margin toward zero.
